blocks.content: This chapter covers Jharkhand-specific welfare/development schemes and its tourism circuit, which spans wildlife, religious pilgrimage, waterfalls and industrial-heritage tourism (Jamshedpur).

items: Abua Awas Yojana — a Jharkhand state housing scheme launched to provide pucca (permanent) houses to eligible rural households, functioning alongside the central Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.

Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana — a state welfare scheme providing direct monthly financial assistance to eligible women, a flagship welfare initiative of the current Hemant Soren government, expanded and re-emphasised during the 2024 Assembly election campaign.

Sarna Dharm Code demand — a significant ongoing political demand from Jharkhand's tribal communities and the state government (which passed a resolution supporting it) seeking a separate religious-code classification ('Sarna') for indigenous tribal faith practitioners in the Census, distinct from existing Hindu/other religious categories — the demand remains pending before the Union Government as of the most recent developments.
Central flagship schemes (Ayushman Bharat, PM Awas Yojana, Jal Jeevan Mission, PM-KISAN) have been extended to Jharkhand alongside these state-specific initiatives.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The Sarna Dharm Code demand — seeking separate Census religious-code recognition for indigenous tribal faith (distinct from Hinduism or other listed religions) — is a live, frequently tested current-affairs topic specific to Jharkhand and neighbouring tribal-majority states, reflecting the tribal-identity themes running through this entire book.

cells: State capital; Rock Garden, Tagore Hill, and gateway to nearby waterfalls (Hundru Falls, Dassam Falls, Jonha Falls) on the Ranchi Plateau's rivers
India's first major planned industrial city (Chapter 6); Jubilee Park, Tata Steel Zoological Park
Baidyanath Dham Jyotirlinga temple; major Hindu pilgrimage centre (Chapter 9)
Jainism's most sacred pilgrimage site (Chapter 9); also a trekking destination given its status as Jharkhand's highest peak
Hill station on the western plateau, popular for sunrise/sunset viewpoints, sometimes called the 'Queen of Chotanagpur'

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Netarhat is popularly nicknamed the 'Queen of Chotanagpur' — a frequently tested tourism-nickname fact for this hill-station destination on Jharkhand's western plateau.

items: Abua Awas Yojana (state housing scheme) and Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana (women's welfare) are flagship current state schemes.
Sarna Dharm Code demand: seeks separate Census religious-code recognition for indigenous tribal faith; remains pending before the Union Government.
Key tourism destinations: Ranchi (waterfalls), Jamshedpur (industrial heritage), Deoghar (Baidyanath Dham), Parasnath Hill (Jain pilgrimage), Betla National Park, Netarhat ('Queen of Chotanagpur').
